items.headline: Musk's dates: a Terafab test chip by June, Optimus doing chores in 12–18 months

items.headline: The numbers behind the tech washout
items.summary: Goldman Sachs prime data shows hedge funds' net momentum exposure fell from about 60% of equity at the peak to 8%, and the weeks before Nov. 13 saw the heaviest net selling of global tech in nine years, @aleabitoreddit noted. @ParadisLabs added that the pace of selling since early October is the fastest in ten years on a trailing six-week basis, led by semis and chip equipment.

items.author: Paul Millerd
items.text:
The rise of the 10x content marketer 

In the past couple of months with the latest models, I’ve been able to create viral content across almost every medium: YouTube, IG, X and LinkedIn. And I’m doing it in less time and having more fun.

In the past 10 years, the way to win on content was to outspend your competition.  Hire huge content teams. Spend on paid and organic reach. That may still be the case.  Money will still matter.

But it meant that if you were someone like me who just didn’t have the financial capital or business model to generate all the cash you needed you were outta luck. 

I’ve been creating online for more than a decade. My entire approach is designed around actually enjoy enjoying it. I experiment with different platforms but always quit if I’m not having fun.

This is the first time I’ve been excited to create a very wide range of content. With AI I can eliminate almost all the painful administrative or tactical things. I hated (and why people always outsource this).  Things like scheduling, analytics, autoreply, campaigns, ads, video editing, b roll management, format design, templates, design styles, trend following - almost all of it is probably lower value work that we thought and is now “solved”.  

I see a clear path to growing a longform and short form video audience now.  

I think this is going to be a rough period for many influencer teams.  There has been somewhat of a moat on video and YouTube because it was so hard to do it well.  In the past two months I’ve been in a rapid learning loop. It’s wild how fast I’m learning. 

I don’t have grand ambitions to grow a massive audience, but it’s very clear that AI native content people are going to be in a massive advantage over clunky human teams.

If the content people aren’t using AI, it’s going to be very hard to keep them. 

These teams are going to shift to supermarkets or what I’m calling a 10x content marketer here. 

You want a cracked systems thinker who’s a strategist and can get their hands dirty across all domains. They’ll be shaping the story energy and campaigns across media. 

I’m not talking automated posting.  I’m talking about hands on and detailed but on the things that matter.  Automated
Replies are soulless. But having creative energy injected into your content with a clear point of view all while enjoying doing it? That will win. 

Maybe you want a second person running the tooling but I suspect a lot of teams will shrink this year. 

It will be very interesting to see how this shakes out.

items.author: Serenity
items.text:
Now that we're close to 2027 it's a good idea to stress test downside scenarios where you have:

1. Capex cuts past 2028 
2. Stranded Compute / DC Slowdowns 
3. Finance deterioration (base case)
4. 2x+ rate hikes

Working in parallel and see what happens with valuations of AI longs. 

If you see acceleration despite all 4, I'd argue that's an opportunity. 

> Next-gen of photonics is one of the rare segments with an extreme rise in optical content and ASPs that can offset aggregate capex cuts. 

Everyone’s moving into that space, including Elon Musk doing M&A, Marvell, Samsung and others with M&A… and we haven’t seen economic impact on emerging architectures even hit players from Celestial to Ayar + their suppliers yet. 

If we look at a scenario where there's excess GPUs but power constraints:

We might see slowdown in aggregate accelerator/GPU/ASIC procurement, but your optical engines + light sources + switches players see acceleration.

Especially as incentive to replace power inefficient networking... since different (cheap BOM) optical architectures improves GPU utilization or even HBM requirements.  

So value migrates to players more high-beta to architectural shifts. 

If Celestial projections are $500m -> $1B, and we expect -30% aggregate capex cuts, I'd argue we'd still see upward revisions from Celestial over the next 2 years.

But financing with #3 matters a lot as seen with $AAOI dropping off of a $550M, vs. $COHR getting prepayments for capacity expansion from their customers. 

Companies that rely on external foundries might be less sensitive to #3 since they're not as capex intensive. 

On the other hand, companies in sectors have a lot of floating interest like certain Neoclouds, and require further financing might be the most impacted. 

> Legacy and specialty memory is a different cycle that markets conflate with AI capex.

If consumer demand weakens but at the same time, players like Windbond exits DDR2, pricing durability is longer than markets expect. 

> Wafer/substrate procurement such as ABF, SOI, InP are low cost but large downstream destruction if not secured, so we’ll likely see acceleration here as seen with $NVDA earnings call. 

> qualification cycle players within bottlenecks remain very compelling, since first revenue in a large TAM, relative to MC is material to that company. 

If a company is valued at $400m then they get a $200m of orders, it's more asymmetrical to a certain company than a rounding error to a $50B incumbent revenue. 
_

There’s period of times where prices are dislocated from fundamentals from leveraged players getting wiped. I’d argue that time is now. 

I disagree with a lot of the stupid "it's over takes" but I agree it's a good idea to haircut future capex expectations and forward valuations due to financing tightening + macro. 

It's also good idea to see the nuances and stress test downside cases. 

But TLDR: I'd argue next phase of AI infrastructure is going to be increasingly disconnected from aggregate AI capex growth. 

I just personally wrote 4 things I'm using to stress test jointly some of the names I'm looking at, so I'm more comfortable waiting things out... despite seeing hedge funds getting liquidated left and right and overwhelming short positioning. 

I personally see acceleration in more narrow parts of the supply chain, while markets treat the entire AI trade as one.  

We'll see how things play out on longer horizons.

items.author: Wall St Engine
items.text:
$500B NVIDIA CHIP-FINANCING PLAN HAS DEPLOYED ZERO CAPITAL, WITH NO DEALS EXPECTED BEFORE 2027: WSJ

In August, $NVDA announced a partnership with Apollo, Blackstone, BlackRock, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs and KKR to mobilize $500B to help customers like OpenAI, Anthropic and smaller AI cloud companies finance chip purchases.

But the agreement was only a few-page memorandum of understanding. None of the firms was obligated to raise any money, and no capital has been deployed.

Jensen Huang had initially pushed for an even larger $1T financing program, partly to support Nvidia's valuation as its earnings grew but its valuation multiple declined.

He accelerated the effort after Apollo and Blackstone helped rival Broadcom arrange $35B in chip financing for Anthropic.

The biggest obstacle has been Nvidia's willingness to guarantee the loans:

Nvidia was willing to provide credit support covering up to 25% of project costs.

Broadcom provided residual-value guarantees covering about 85% of Anthropic's $35B Project Big Sky and just under 75% of its $63B Project North Star.

As lenders have become more cautious about AI financing, they have pushed Nvidia to offer greater protection.

Nvidia has also been pulling back its financial guarantees. Earlier, reports of a proposed $250B Nvidia backstop for an OpenAI data center sent $NVDA shares down 5%, prompting Nvidia to cut its initial commitment in half.

Interim CEO Colette Kress has since signaled that future investments and guarantees will be evaluated more strictly.

Talks on the partnership's first chip-backed financing deal are still underway, but nothing is expected to close before 2027.

Apollo CEO Marc Rowan warned that without Nvidia providing financial guarantees, a large number of neocloud companies could lose access to capital.

Leopold Aschenbrenner, the 25-year-old founder of Situational Awareness, is reportedly planning a comeback just four months after leveraged AI-stock bets nearly destroyed his hedge fund.

Dubbed “Situational Awareness 2.0,” the plan could involve renewed leverage and fresh investor capital, according to the Financial Times.

“So this is kind of a long answer, but we are working on Grok 4.8 right now. It’s in the RL phase. And we do sort of periodic soft releases under Grok Bot.”

“So what you’ll experience with Grok Bot at times is actually various versions of Grok under the hood that we’re testing to determine its usefulness. Is it solving the user’s problem? And then using that data, whether it did or did not solve the problem, to improve Grok.”

quoted.author: Fireside Alpha
quoted.text:
Elon Musk says xAI might now have “the best training stack software in the world” after rewriting everything from scratch over six to eight months

“And this meant rewriting the entire training, RL and inference stack from scratch, versus using JAX and SGLang, which is sort of kind of freeware from Google, more or less, but not as good as what they’ve got internally by far. So you just can’t build world class AI using mediocre freeware, to state the obvious.”

“So we’ve been rewriting the entire training stack. When I say the entire training stack, I mean everything. We’re using primarily C and some C++, because we wanna get as close to the bare metal as possible in order to extract the highest performance from the hardware. The more layers of software abstraction that you have, the less performant your code will be. And it also tends to be more of a black box, where you’re not quite sure what’s going on with the third-party software.”

“So now this is happening very fast by normal standards. It’s sort of happening over the course of maybe six to eight months. And now I feel we’ve actually got the software to be very good. I think we might have the best training stack software in the world, and you’ll see the dividends of that, the fruit of that, in the models that come out.”

Financial media is panicking over headlines claiming $NVDA just pulled the rug out from under $CRWV, $NBIS, $IREN, and other neoclouds.

items.author: Northwise Project
items.text:
Microsoft $MSFT received more GPU capacity at Vineland in November. The last deliveries are now due in Q2 2027.

DataOne took some of its temporary gas generators offline before Bloom Energy $BE could replace the power. The first fuel cells are running now. How fast that output grows will help determine how many clusters Nebius $NBIS can hand over in December. The company expects to have delivered more than half of the contracted capacity by year-end.

We put the power handoff and revised delivery dates on one timeline in the updated Vineland report.
items.image_alt: Timeline of the power handoff at Vineland, New Jersey. DataOne began cutting temporary generation in late Q3 2026 before Bloom’s fuel cells could replace it. Bloom was generating power by November. Nebius expects Microsoft to receive more than half of its contracted capacity by the end of 2026, with the remaining deliveries scheduled for Q2 2027.
